PullRequest.Title: agentHost: fix context size picker for Codex harness
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- surface Copilot-backed model context-size options in the Codex harness
- forward the selected token window to Codex app-server thread start/resume configuration
- reload materialized threads when context size changes while preserving conversation history
- share the context-size schema helper with the Copilot harness
- add regression coverage that verifies context size and thinking level reach both runtime boundaries together

## Verification

- 123 focused Codex tests pass (64 prewarm/session tests and 59 model-refresh tests)
- 9 focused Copilot model-configuration tests pass
- focused ESLint passes
- `npm run transpile-client` passes
- `git diff --check` passes
- launch + DAP verification with `GPT-5.6 Sol Fast (Internal only)`:
  - Codex UI showed `Max 1M` and completed a prompt; app-server received `thread/start.config.model_context_window = 922000`, `turn/start.effort = "max"`, and `collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort = "max"`
  - Copilot UI showed `Max 1M` and completed a prompt; the launcher resolved `{ thinkingLevel: "max", contextSize: 922000 }` to `reasoningEffort = "max"` and `contextTier = "long_context"`
  - at the actual Copilot SDK JSON-RPC boundary, `session.create` carried model `gpt-5.6-sol-fast`, `reasoningEffort: "max"`, and `contextTier: "long_context"`
- `922000` is the expected usable input window: the model reserves 128K output tokens from its 1.05M total window, while the picker intentionally formats the tier as `1M`

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex model-catalog refresh after authentication or a scheduled refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing refresh awaits the Copilot model-catalog network request and Codex catalog refresh in parallel before publishing models; the diff adds only local billing normalization reuse and schema construction after the same response arrives.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the authoritative Copilot model catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per existing refresh attempt, independent of model count; retries retain the existing bounded backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog request and refresh sequencing occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the refreshed model list is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh native Codex models through the existing app-server path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing refresh operation per catalog refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with the Copilot catalog fetch and is awaited before publishing the combined list.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of returned picker-eligible models; each model receives one constant-size context schema at most.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two authoritative catalog refreshes remain under the existing sequencer and run through Promise.all; the diff adds no request concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resulting schemas are retained in the existing in-memory _models catalog. Warm reads use that catalog; retry/backoff and last-known-good behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed map body and unchanged request placement directly establish constant local work per returned model.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The model count varies by entitlement, but schema work is linear with a realistically small catalog and has no added boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new network/subprocess fan-out, unbounded retention, or critical-path scheduling change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating, restoring, or forking a Codex chat with a selected context size
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing thread/start, thread/resume, or thread/fork IPC must complete before the chat can proceed; the diff adds one scalar model_context_window field to the existing request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One thread/start per existing materialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same thread/start occurred without model_context_window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the backing chat is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One thread/resume per existing cold restore or required reload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold restored sessions already resumed; the request now carries the selected context window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One thread/fork per user fork, plus the pre-existing rollback only when trailing turns must be removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fork request occurred without the context-window scalar.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected model configuration per chat operation; request cardinality does not scale with history items or workspace files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-chat/session lifecycle sequencing remains in force. Each operation issues one authoritative thread request; no new parallel burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The offered-size validation reads the warm in-memory model catalog with a linear lookup over the small model list. Cold model loading is already completed before supported selections are exposed; there is no new cache miss boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed launch sites spread a constant-size object into already-existing IPC payloads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long sessions can retain more provider context when the user chooses the larger tier, but that is the feature's explicit compaction-horizon choice rather than duplicated host work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: serialization growth is constant and boundary cardinality is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changing Codex context size on a materialized thread, then sending the next message
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A real context-size change marks the thread for reload. On the next send, thread/unsubscribe and thread/resume are awaited before turn/start so app-server applies the launch-only compaction boundary; the asynchronous MCP inventory refresh is not awaited by the turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unsubscribe the loaded thread so conflicting launch overrides can be replaced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one thread/unsubscribe before the next successful resume, even if the picker changes repeatedly before sending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same-provider model/config changes did not trigger this unsubscribe unless another existing launch-only setting independently required reload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on the first turn after an actual context-size change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the same persisted history with the new model_context_window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced thread/resume after the change, with existing reconnect retries only on connection replacement/failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No context-size feature existed in Codex, so this reload was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before turn/start; required because app-server ignores conflicting overrides on an already-loaded subscribed thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List MCP server status after the resumed thread loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous listing per resume, paginated by the existing server cursor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This listing already followed every resume; the diff causes one additional resume/listing only when context size actually changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget after resume; not awaited before turn preparation, though it shares the IPC transport.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the provider turn after configuration is current.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The turn started directly when no other reload condition applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still follows required session preparation; request count is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual context-size changes for one live chat, not messages or history items. Multiple changes before the next send collapse into the same needsResume/unsubscribeBeforeResume booleans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The session resumePromise coalesces concurrent resume demand, and the send path waits for one resume before the turn. The MCP inventory list is started asynchronously after resume and may paginate according to server count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm turns with unchanged context perform no reload. A changed value invalidates the loaded thread configuration once; after resume, subsequent turns reuse the loaded thread. The selected size is validated against the warm model schema.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed comparison, boolean coalescing, resume loop, and test-observed request sequence directly establish the path and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: IPC duration and MCP page count depend on app-server state and configured servers, but the first-turn delay after a change is bounded to one coalesced reload and is necessary to apply the requested launch-only setting.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added one-time latency is bounded, coalesced, deferred until use, and required to preserve history while applying a launch-only context setting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot-backed model schema, session creation, and live model reconfiguration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing SDK session.create and session.setModel control-plane calls remain the runtime boundaries; the shared helper only preserves the existing Copilot schema behavior and forwards context tier together with reasoning effort.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an SDK session with contextTier and reasoningEffort.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing SDK session.create per materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The numeric context selection was already mapped to contextTier; the diff moves only the key/helper ownership and expands test coverage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited as before; payload gains no unbounded data.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply model, effort, context tier, and auto tier to a live SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing setModel control-plane call per selection update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same call already accepted and received contextTier; production behavior is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited in the existing per-chat sequencer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One model selection per session creation or user/turn selection update; context data is one numeric enum value resolved to one tier string.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot changes remain serialized by the existing per-chat queue. No new calls or fan-out are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Long-context windows and free-tier membership are read from existing in-memory model metadata. Session creation is cold once; repeated selections use the materialized session and existing queue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the production diff is a helper/key extraction with unchanged callers and boundary count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-side cost of deliberately selected extended context varies with conversation length, but the Copilot path's runtime mechanism is pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression and no qualifying regression fix; this path is behavior-preserving.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced catalog refresh, Codex start/fork/resume, mid-session context changes, MCP inventory refresh, and Copilot SDK boundaries. The only added boundary work is one coalesced Codex unsubscribe/resume on the first turn after an actual context-size change; it is required by app-server launch-only semantics and does not repeat on warm unchanged turns. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
